fields.subnational_unit: one village in a rural sub-county of Bushenyi District, south-west Uganda (name withheld)
fields.population: 21 duty bearers (politicians and technocrats) linked to the village and 92 water users aged 25+ in a small 'typical' village; district performs above national average (93% vs 68% safe water access; 90% vs 84% functionality)
fields.sample_size: 92 water-user survey respondents, 21 duty-bearer interviews, one focus group; single village in one district (a 'most likely' case)
fields.effect_measure: social network analysis (UCINET, SPSS) comparing the actual information-sharing network with two theoretical networks built from the Local Governments Act 1997, the 2011 National Framework for O&M of Rural Water Supplies and Quin et al. (2011); centrality, reciprocity, correlation of networks
fields.effect_estimate: Actual information exchange is more intense than the legislated one-way reporting chain and resembles Quin's theoretical network, but is more centralised and less reciprocal than either; the district water officer is more central than expected; the main bottleneck is information between higher (district, sub-county) and lower (parish, village) levels, not between political and administrative actors; the village chairperson is the key broker upward; water user committees play a limited role. Reported quantities are network metrics for one village, not effect sizes.
fields.model_type: social network analysis (descriptive; QAP-style comparison with theoretical networks)
fields.study_design: single-village case study using network survey, key-informant interviews, focus group and document review (mixed methods; not a cross-sectional analytical study)
fields.section: Full text (Commonwealth Journal of Local Governance 22:7021): Research design and methodology; networks among government actors and with users; Conclusion
fields.exact_location: Research design and methodology p4-6 (case selection, sources, sample); network results p7-20; Conclusion p21

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a one-village social network case study in Bushenyi District, Uganda (92 water users, 21 duty bearers), read in full text 2026-10-04. The legislated reporting chain under the Local Governments Act 1997 is compared with actual information flows: more centralised and less reciprocal than envisaged, with district-parish/village flows as the bottleneck and a limited role for water user committees. Single village, no effect sizes.
